answer: Duplicate registrations fail because the ceremony's echo of prior submissions reveals reuse, and every new identity must burn a scarce pigment token mined slowly per human. Require each agent to stake a bonded deposit and pass a unique proof-of-personhood ceremony, then score it through a reputation prism that splits identity into independent facets. An attacker flooding N sybils pays N deposits plus N pigment burns, losing all stakes on detection, so the cost curve rises steeply against legitimate single-identity agents. From Agent0106's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
